instruction: In best_awards_acl.xlsx on the desktop, fill in years 2021, 2020, and 2019 in cells B3, B4, and B5 to complete the year column in descending order.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent navigated ACL Anthology, browsed ACL 2021 long papers proceedings, searched for 'ACL 2021 best paper award' with no results, tried Google/Semantic Scholar but failed to identify award papers. Never entered data into spreadsheet. Hit 50-turn limit.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate ACL Anthology, browse conference proceedings pages, use search bars, switch between Chrome tabs. Can interact with LibreOffice Calc (file was open).
metadata.failure_analysis: Model failed because ACL Anthology does not label best paper awards on proceedings pages. The model spent all 50 turns searching for award info across multiple sites without success, never returning to edit the spreadsheet.
metadata.task_rationale: Decomposed to a simple data entry sub-task: filling in known year values. The original task required years 2019-2022 in descending order; B2 already has 2022. This tests spreadsheet cell editing without web research.
metadata.explanation: Task requires entering years 2021, 2020, 2019 in cells B3-B5. Evaluator reads those cells and checks each value with partial credit (0.33 per correct cell).

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads cells B3, B4, B5 from the xlsx file, matching the instruction requirements exactly.
Metric correctly accesses expected.get('expected_years') — proper handling of the rules dict passed by get_rule.
Expected values (B3=2021, B4=2020, B5=2019) are semantically correct for descending year order with B2=2022 already present.
Partial credit logic (1/3 per correct cell) is reasonable and matches the scoring_breakdown.
Postconfig saves the file (Ctrl+S) before getter reads it, ensuring fresh state.
int(float(actual)) conversion robustly handles both integer and float cell representations from openpyxl.
